amendments.rule: **Hebrew has no verb *to have*, so an English *have* is a recasting and belongs to whatever made the clause possessive.** Where `הָיָה` is present it is the existential and takes the *have* itself, its preposition goes `unrepresented` under rule 40, and the suffix takes the subject pronoun: `וַיְהִי לוֹ נָשִׁים` → *he had* … *wives* puts *had* on `הָיָה` and *he* on the suffix. Where the clause is verbless, the possessive preposition is what makes it possessive and carries the *have*: `לָהֶם מִסְגְּרוֹת` → *they had panels* puts *had* on `לְ` and *they* on the suffix, and `שָׁפְרָה עָלָי` → *I have a goodly heritage* puts *have* on `עַל` and *I* on the suffix. Where neither is present, a possessive suffix can be the possession by itself and takes the supplied verb with its pronoun: `טוֹבָתִי בַּל עָלֶיךָ` → *I have no good beyond thee* gives the suffix *I have*, headed on the pronoun. Another finite verb in the clause does not qualify merely by being finite. `שָׁפְרָה` is not a copula: the ASV renders it by the attributive *goodly*, which is its lexeme, so the *have* is not its. **But a verb the ASV has itself rendered by the *have* does qualify, and the same subtraction decides it.** Where the Hebrew writes a verb of falling or allotment and the English writes *have* in its place — `יִפְּלוּ בְנַחֲלָה` → *they shall have inheritance* — dropping the word leaves that verb with no rendering at all, so the *have* is the verb's own together with the subject pronoun rule 17 keeps there, and a preposition beside it whose relation the ASV has left unstated goes `unrepresented` under rule 40. **And where nothing in the clause makes it possessive, the word is not to be placed at all.** A clause that writes no `הָיָה`, no possessive preposition, no suffix and no verb the *have* renders has no morpheme to carry it: `יוֹסֵף חֲבָלִים` → *Joseph* ***shall have two*** *portions* leaves the supplied verb its own `added` unit under rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause, together with any numeral, subject or object the ASV supplies alongside it, while the possessed noun keeps only its own word. Do not fold such a word into that noun, into a neighbouring clause's verb, or into a preposition standing elsewhere in the verse to avoid the `added`, for the reason rule 42 gives about a surplus *and*: it is written beside those renderings rather than inside one of them. Test by subtraction, as in rule 16 — drop the *have* and ask which morpheme has lost its rendering. If only the possession relation is gone, the *have* is the preposition's or the suffix's; if a written verb is left with nothing, it is that verb's; and if nothing in the clause is diminished but a possession the English has supplied, it is `added`.
amendments.why: Rule 43's opening sentence tells a reader the *have* belongs to whatever made the clause possessive and then enumerates three hosts, with no exit for a clause that has none — which is how EZK.47.13's `יוֹסֵף חֲבָלִים` → *Joseph shall have two portions* arrives, a verbless allotment clause with no `הָיָה`, no preposition and no suffix. Left as it stood, the rule invites hunting for a host and folding the word onto `חֲבָלִים` or reaching across the verse; the added clause routes it to rule 20's existing supplied-lexical-verb ruling on the parallel Joshua allotment formula, so it harmonizes 43 with 20 rather than inventing anything. The second addition guards the opposite error, which the same chapter shows at EZK.47.22: `יִפְּלוּ בְנַחֲלָה` → *they shall have inheritance* is a written verb the ASV renders by *have*, and rule 43's bare sentence that another finite verb 'does not qualify merely by being finite' reads as a blanket prohibition until the subtraction test is applied to it. Both branches are attested in this chapter and neither touches the corpus's 81 `לְ` → *had*, 26 → *have* and 18 → *hath* units, every one of which has a preposition present.

conventions: Boundary-formula closing. The refrain we-'et pe'at X -> 'This is the X side' (47.17, 47.18, 47.19) writes no conjunction, no subject and no verb: the waw and the object marker are each their own unrepresented unit, the supplied 'This' is added under rule 17, and pe'ah as the clause's predicate carries the construction-supplied 'is the' under rules 15 and 20. Where the Hebrew does write its own demonstrative, as zo't pe'at-yam in 47.20, 'This' is aligned to it and nothing is added. Read the clause for a demonstrative morpheme before placing the word, and do not reach for the object marker to carry it.

derek in this chapter is always rendered 'by the way' (47.2 three times, 47.15), so the construct noun keeps its own English word 'way' and the supplied 'by' joins it under rule 33, while the rectum keeps the relational 'of' under rule 19 and a present article takes the written 'the' (47.15) where an absent one leaves it to the noun's expression (47.2). Rule 19's derek -> 'toward' clause is not engaged anywhere here: it governs a construct whose whole rendering is the preposition, and none of these is.

The measuring walk's depth phrases - me 'ophsayim (47.3), mayim birkayim (47.4), me motnayim (47.4), me sahu (47.5) - all give the entire supplied relational frame ('that were to the', 'to swim in') to the second noun, headed on that noun. The rule cited follows MACULA's morphology, rule 19 where the first noun is construct and rule 33 where it is absolute and the second stands in apposition, but the unit boundaries and the head are the same in both, so the morphological difference is not a reason to divide them differently.

Directive he in the boundary list is fused with its host wherever the ASV writes a single English word for the pair, including where that word is not itself directional - qadimah -> 'east' (47.18), temanah -> 'south' (47.19) - and is marked unrepresented only where another morpheme has already taken the word that carries the direction, as lipe'at saponah -> 'On the north side' and lebo' sedadah -> 'unto the entrance of Zedad' (both 47.15). Rule 32 is read here as a one-English-word test, not a test of whether the English word is directional; the chapter is uniform on it and 47.1's 'eastward' is the same test coming out the other way.

report: Read all 61 candidate groups, then the whole dump end to end for the splits the table cannot show (added units, supplied English). No construction is analysed two ways without something in the source licensing the difference, so patches is empty.

Near-misses checked and cleared. (a) mizzeh umizzeh: 47.7 'the one side ... the other' vs 47.12 'this side ... that side' - the ASV's wording differs and both units head by rule 31's subtraction. (b) we-lo': 47.11 splits into 'But' (waw) + 'not' because the ASV writes two words in two places, while 47.12 fuses 'neither' on the negative - rule 35's one-word condition read off the ASV, and the corpus records both treatments in quantity. (c) Directive he: fused wherever the ASV writes one word (47.1, 2, 9, 17, 18, 19), unrepresented only where another morpheme already took the direction (47.8 s028 after 'el, both tokens in 47.15). (d) Water-depth appositions: 47.3, 47.4 and 47.5 all give the whole supplied frame ('that were to the', 'to swim in') to the second noun; the note cites rule 19 or rule 33 according to whether MACULA makes the first noun construct or absolute, and the division is identical either way. (e) bammayim -> 'through' (preposition present, 47.3 and 47.4a) versus 'caused ... to pass through' (no preposition, 47.4b) is rule 44's supplied-preposition clause, correctly counted. (f) Article placement in hayyam haggadol, hayyam haqqadmoni, hakkatep hayemanit and ketep habbayit hayemanit is uniform under rule 47: a present article takes the written 'the', the construct takes a supplied one, agreement articles go unrepresented.

Added units cross-checked in both directions, since the candidate table is blind to them. Every supplied 'the', copula and adverbial function word in this chapter is folded into the morpheme that licenses it, and the 14 added units are exactly the cases where no such morpheme stands: no waw (47.5 'and'), no object morpheme (47.6 'this', 47.23 'him'), no source nominal (47.8, 47.9, and the three 'This' of 47.17-19), a supplied head noun as well as its function word (47.2 'of the gate', 47.18 'north', 47.19 'of Egypt', 47.20 'south'), and nothing possessive at all (47.13 'shall have two'). The one 'This' that is aligned, 47.20, is the one clause that writes zo't. Nowhere does the chapter fold a supplied word into a neighbouring rendering in one verse and mark its twin added in another.

BSB disagreements: none is a genuine error. The 16 Td and 10 R rows are the documented convention difference (BSB attaches an article or a preposition to its phrase where the ASV writes nothing for it), and each ASV unrepresented reading is forced by the English actually written - 47.3 ba'ammah has no preposition in 'a thousand cubits', 47.5 la'abor has no infinitive marker in 'could not pass through', 47.16 and 47.18 are rule 26's repeated ben, 47.22 s037 writes 'inheritance' bare, 47.23 'itto is an unwritten resumptive. The three waw rows (47.3, 47.17, 47.18) are connective counts: each of those clauses has one more waw than the ASV has connectives, and the written 'and' is placed by the pair of phrases it stands between. The To, Sd and 'adonay-suffix rows are contract defaults (rules 16, 32, 22).

One judgment considered and left standing: 47.14 keeps the object marker of the nasa'-yad idiom outside the noncompositional 'I sware' unit, marking it unrepresented under rule 16's default, whereas the two corpus units of the same idiom (EXO.6.8, NUM.14.30) fold the marker into the fusion. Both readings are defensible under rules 16 and 30, the verse's note names the reading it took, and a single-verse judgment already argued is not a cross-verse split; recorded here so a later reader can see it was weighed rather than missed.
